prompt:
Image 1 is a finished game sprite sheet whose drawing is right: keep exactly its camera (high above and in front, looking down at about 40 degrees), the direction every figure faces, every figure's pose, size and position in its cell, the 4 by 4 grid and the flat pure magenta (#FF00FF) background. Image 1 shows a levy spearman of the same nation.
Image 2 is a painted portrait from the same game, a reference for the painting hand and the materials only: do not paint that person, and do not copy its dark background, its candlelight or its framing.

A previous attempt at this sheet failed: the surcoat was added by an edit of another sheet and four cells drifted from their poses. This time the base is a different sheet whose every pose is right.

Repaint every figure of Image 1 as a different soldier, the same soldier in every cell. Keep each figure's pose, the position of its arms, legs and weapon, and its outline as close as the new kit allows. He is now a big, broad heavy infantryman: the raised hood becomes a closed bark helm crowned with a ring of short thorns and a deep green leaf crest running front to back; his sleeves, bracers and wrapped legs become thick black-brown bark plates studded with short thorns on the shoulders, arms and legs; the short hooded cloak becomes a heavy deep bottle-green mantle across his shoulders; the long deep bottle-green surcoat stays over his chest and belly to just below the knees, held by a thorn-studded belt; the spear becomes a long halberd with a curved thorn-shaped blade, a back hook and a spike, held exactly where the spear is held. Every figure keeps the outline of Image 1: the same silhouette, the same arms, legs and weapon in the same places, the same size and the same place in its cell; only the clothes, armour, skin and the weapon's own shape change. Do not re-pose any figure, even where its pose looks unusual for this soldier.

The soldier: A Briar Guard, heavy infantry: thick armour of black-brown bark plates studded with short thorns on the shoulders, arms and legs; a sleeveless surcoat of deep bottle-green cloth that covers his whole chest and belly from the collar down to just below the knees, front and back, split at the front below the belt so the legs can stride and held at the waist by a thorn-studded belt, worn over the bark plates of the body; a closed bark helm crowned with a ring of thorns and a deep green leaf crest; a heavy deep bottle-green mantle across the shoulders and the upper back; a long halberd with a curved thorn-shaped blade, a back hook and a spike. No shield, no antlers. Big and broad.

Side colour: the leaf crest, the heavy mantle and the long surcoat are cloth dyed deep bottle green: the colour of jade or of a green glass bottle held to the light, a clear and fairly saturated cool green; never leaf-green, olive, grey or blackish, never as blue as teal. These are large, clean, unbroken areas that face the sky and the camera, so that a packed block of these soldiers reads as that colour from far away.

Paint him in the hand of the game's painted portraits: painterly oil on a wood panel, visible directional brushwork, a muted earthy palette, small crisp highlights on metal edges and a thin bright rim of light along the upper-left edges; nothing glows unless the description says so. Keep the daylight of Image 1 (a high sun from the upper left, a cool fill on the lower right). Realistic adult proportions; no cartoon, no thick outlines.

Facing, again: every figure faces exactly as in Image 1, toward us and to the lower left, the hit and the falling figures included; the fleeing figures run as in Image 1.

Background: one flat pure magenta (#FF00FF) colour fills the whole image with no gradient, texture, floor or shadow. No magenta, pink or purple anywhere on the figures. Never: text, labels, grid lines, borders, a floor, cast shadows, blood, extra people, cropped or overlapping figures.
